critic_text:
The six runtime files and `check.py`'s child-path ban are aimed at the right defect. The records skip, the revert evidence, and the docs half of the spec are not.

**1. The records exemption is the wrong shape.** Spec text for `check.py` is: forbid any child of `~/.claude/plugins`, allow the parent as a Glob root, allowlist two docs for `marketplaces` only, exclude itself. The implementation adds a whole-subtree `continue` on `.claude/specs/` and `.claude/runs/` (`rel.startswith(records)`). That is a spec deviation, not an implementation detail. `.claude/runs/` as immutable transcripts is defensible. `.claude/specs/` is not: those files are read as instructions in this kind of repo, and a spec that narrates the old Glob is exactly the text an agent will copy. A tighter rule that would change my mind: allowlist the specific files that must name both spellings, or permit a child name in records only when the same file also names the parent-root procedure. Skipping every future path under those prefixes means the defect has a green place to live.

**2. Yes, the same hole is still in this diff — it was made permanent.** `_install_paths` still iterates `tracked()`. The check went green at commit and red once specs were tracked; the response was to stop reading that tree. That is not closing "guard green against files it was not reading." It is encoding it. `e2e.py` has a second copy of the hole: a closed list of six paths, so a seventh runtime file with the old Glob never fails `test_bundled_files_are_resolved_not_guessed`. `check.py` would catch a named child if that seventh file is tracked and not under records; it would not catch a wrong procedure that never names a child.

**3. Do not remove the multiple-match STOP.** A one-layout machine cannot fire it, and deleting it reopens guessing — the failure mode this unit exists to kill. What is not acceptable is calling it a tested guarantee. The assertion is `"more than one" in body.lower()`, uncoupled from STOP. Constitution Article 3 is not met for that branch: the behaviour was not watched failing on a tree that actually produced two matches. Fixture-only text can ship as a conservative instruction; it cannot be counted as an executed branch.

**Assertions are not all real.** Recorded revert: one restored runtime file fails 2 of 24 e2e checks. Four claims are made per file (parent root, middle `**`, STOP, multiple-match). Two stayed green on a deliberately broken file. The parent check (`"~/.claude/plugins`" in body or "~/.claude/plugins " in body`) matches any other mention of the parent; the old SKILL.md already contained `STOP and report`. So the load-bearing revert signal is middle `**` plus `"more than one"`, not the four-step procedure. `check.py` injection evidence (old literal → 1 problem; Windows + `cache` in an allowlisted doc → 3; bare parent passes) is the actual guard for the defect class.

**The omitted seven diffs do not generalise.** Spec splits eight files into six runtime procedures and two docs that must not contract the layout. The brief shows one runtime edit and calls the rest "mechanical and identical." That category error is how a doc that hardcodes `marketplaces/...` as the path to type would hide. Nothing in `check.py` or `e2e.py` asserts observed-not-contracted; the allowlist *permits* `marketplaces` in those two files and does not require the caution.

`test_implementation_stage_matches_the_pipeline` is not this spec. It landed in the same hunk with no fail-first record in this package.

- severity: major — `_install_paths` skips `.claude/specs/` and `.claude/runs/` entirely; spec did not allow that hole, and it is the tracked()-blindness bug made permanent
- severity: major — reverting one runtime file fails 2/24 e2e assertions, so parent-root and STOP were not watched failing on a broken tree
- severity: major — the two docs have no observed-not-contracted assertion and were omitted under an identical-shape claim the spec contradicts
- severity: minor — multiple-match STOP is unexecuted substring text; keep it, but it is not an Article 3 guarantee
- severity: minor — `test_implementation_stage_matches_the_pipeline` is outside this unit and has no fail-first evidence here
verdict: concerns

The implementation is not fully compliant.

The records exemption is too broad for the stated guarantee. `_install_paths()` skips every file under `.claude/specs/` and `.claude/runs/`, so a prohibited child path can exist there without detection. If those are truly non-instructions, that boundary needs an explicit, independently enforced classification; otherwise the exemption contradicts “forbids naming any CHILD.”

The tracked-file gap remains. `for path in tracked()` means any newly created or untracked runtime/documentation file is invisible to the guard. The e2e test reads six hard-coded paths directly, but does not prove that `check.py` audits them. The same commit-time failure can therefore recur for other files.

The e2e assertions are mostly textual presence checks. They do not assert the four-step behavior: exactly one match is used, no match stops, or multiple matches reports all matches. The multiple-match prose may be acceptable as shipped behavior, but its actual branch remains unexecuted and unverified. The omitted seven prose edits also cannot be independently judged from this diff.

- severity: major — The records exemption allows prohibited install paths to escape the required check.
- severity: major — `tracked()` leaves new untracked runtime files outside the install-path guard.
- severity: major — E2E checks wording, not the required resolution semantics or reporting behavior.

verdict: concerns

## Does the implementation do what the spec says

The core mechanism conforms. The regex `\.claude[/\\]plugins[/\\]([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)` in `check.py` forbids any child segment repo-wide, requires no home prefix (with a documented watched-failing reason), allowlists exactly `INSTALL.md` and `docs/plugin-authoring.md` for the `marketplaces` spelling only — so the expelled `cache` cannot return even there — and excludes itself. The four e2e assertions per runtime file (6 × 4 = 24, matching the brief) map onto the spec's four-step resolution, and the one prose edit shown satisfies all four of its assertions. The two suites compose correctly: e2e pins the parent root, check.py makes it impossible to satisfy e2e while smuggling a child elsewhere in the file.

## The three attack points

**1. The records exemption.** The justification (narration must name both spellings; transcripts are immutable) is real, but the *shape* is wrong. The same function already implements the bounded alternative: `allowed` maps specific files to specific permitted segments. Permitting `{cache, marketplaces}` under `.claude/specs/` would let the narration through while still catching a novel or mistyped child. A whole-subtree skip permits *any* child, forever — and specs are exactly the files an agent resumes work from, so "neither is a file an agent follows" is asserted, not shown. Worst: this was adopted to solve a *transient* problem (specs untracked at commit time; staging + re-running would have caught them, since `git ls-files` reads the index) and the cost is *permanent* — the check is now green against files it refuses to read, which is the hole-class institutionalized rather than fixed.

**2. Is anything still subject to the untracked-file hole?** Yes, structurally. `tracked()` is still index-only; the diff adds no coverage of untracked/staged files and no ordering fix. Every future new file is unread by the guard until tracked. The diff documents the hole in a comment and works around one instance of it permanently, but the class remains open.

**3. The fixture-only multiple-match branch.** Ship it. The spec *requires* the branch ("more than one match → STOP and report all"); removing spec-required defensive text because it hasn't fired would ship an instruction that guesses on ambiguity — strictly worse. But "never fired on a real machine" is a choice, not a necessity: planting a decoy second copy of a plugin under `~/.claude/plugins` and running the Glob exercises the branch on the real install. Record that run or record the gap as chosen.

## Are the assertions real

Mostly, but the Article 3 record has cracks. The recorded revert evidence — "fails 2 of 24" — does not reconcile with the only prose edit shown: reverting the representative file would fail **3** assertions (parent-root, middle `**`, multiple-match), because the old text already contained "STOP and report". The count 2 is consistent only if the reverted file was one of the unseen five whose old text already kept the middle `**` — unverifiable, and the brief doesn't say. Corollary: the "STOP and report" assertion passes on *both* old and new text of the representative file, so it has never been watched failing for that file at all. Similarly "2 injections → 3 problems" is unexplained. And no assertion pins that the two docs actually *contain* the observed-layout statement — the allowance is a ceiling, not a floor; a doc that drops the description passes everything.

## What it breaks

Any tracked file outside the allowlist that legitimately names a child now fails the check — intended, with a actionable message. The real breakage is in the diff's own scope: `test_implementation_stage_matches_the_pipeline` (~35 assertions over AC1–AC7 — slug-vs-ticket-key, flag-set equality, complexity, dry-run, roles, tasks.md, gate count) is an entire test for a *different unit's* contract. The brief's "what the implementation did" claims 24 assertions for install paths and says nothing about this. Whether it's commit pollution or a mis-briefed diff, those guarantees ship in this unit with no watched-failing evidence in this record.

- severity: major — the diff ships test_implementation_stage_matches_the_pipeline (~35 assertions over a different unit's AC1–AC7) that the brief never mentions, with no watched-failing evidence in this record (Article 3).
- severity: major — the .claude/specs/ + .claude/runs/ whole-subtree exemption is a permanent blind spot bought for a transient staging-order problem; the function's own permitted-segment mechanism ({cache, marketplaces}) would allow the narration while still catching a novel child in files agents resume work from.
- severity: minor — watched-failing evidence doesn't reconcile: one-file revert recorded as 2 of 24, but reverting the shown representative edit would fail 3, and its "STOP and report" assertion passed on the old text too (never watched failing there); "2 injections → 3 problems" is likewise unexplained.
- severity: minor — no assertion pins that the two docs actually state the observed layout; the allowlist is a ceiling, so a doc that drops the description entirely passes all gates.
- severity: minor — the multiple-match branch is recorded as never fired though exercisable on a real machine via a decoy second plugin copy under the parent; shipping it is correct (spec-required), but the gap is chosen, not necessary — run the decoy and record it.

verdict: concerns
